name: Engraving
summary: A natural-history copperplate that engraves itself on laid paper: swelling burin lines and cross-hatching build every tone, magnified roundels sit in the margins, roman capitals and italic names label the parts, and a hand-laid watercolour wash arrives last.

palette.use: laid paper: the sheet, its fibres and laid lines
ink: every line, every letter (warm near-black)
the script ink of notes and the subtitle
plate tone inside the pressed plate mark (at 55%)
the pale blue-grey wash (at 50–60%): sky, the blue bar, the scattered glow
the amber wash: the one stronger pigment, used once (the sun)
sparse foxing spots on the paper
the deckled paper slip under a subtitle
an earth wash for ground or a second part (rare)

type.case: roman capitals for titles and labels, italic for names, script for notes
type.emphasis: hierarchy: roman title → italic name → script note; colour never on type

banned: uniform-width lines (they read as pen or vector)
grey fills in the ink: all tone is line density
opaque colour; colour on lettering, rules or paper outside the figure
fades and UI-style slides: lines are cut, text is cut or written, colour blooms
leaders hugging the subject; outline-only parts beside a hatched body
a woodcut, pen sketch, engineering drawing or sepia filter
copying a historic plate, pose, border or title
